dataset.name: Data for Photosynthetic responses to temperature across the tropics: a meta-analytic approach
description: This data package contains raw data, data output, and code of photosynthetic temperature response curves from tropical forests. Data are used in "Photosynthetic responses to temperature across the tropics: a meta-analytic approach". The research investigates how photosynthetic optimum temperatures and shapes of photosynthetic temperature response curves varies across tropical forest climates and growth conditions. Growth climate variables include mean annual temperature, max and max temperature, diurnal temperature range, and aridity index. Meta-analysis combines 18 datasets with representation from Africa, Oceana, North American, and South America. Growth conditions analyzed considers deciduousness, successional status, light conditions, and whether plants are grown in situ or ex situ. All files, except for the raw datafile (Tropical_MetaAnalysis_Master_3.8.22_Edit.csv), have been processed using R code, which is provided.

provider.name: Effects of Hurricane Disturbance and Increased Temperature on Carbon Cycling and Storage of a Puerto Rican Forest: A Mechanistic Investigation of Above- and Belowground Processes

measurementTechnique: We performed a literature search on Web of Science using "photosynthesis" "tropical" "temperature" search terms (last search December 2017). This resulted in 848 studies. We removed 18 replicate studies or conference proceedings, resulting in 830 identified studies. We individually screened all 830 references and excluded any studies that used herbaceous/aquatic/non-plant research, did not include temperature responses with a temperature optimum, modeling articles, review articles, opinion articles, studies without reporting photosynthesis, any study that was not at the leaf level (whole canopy or ecosystem), studies outside of the tropics, or photosynthesis fit to growth temperatures instead of instantaneous temperatures. This resulted in 11 records from Web of Science.

After performing the literature search, we reached out to individual authors to expand our dataset. We were provided three additional unpublished datasets that met our criteria. Authors also provided four additional datasets from published studies that were not identified in our literature search. This resulted in a 18 studies in our final dataset.

We extracted temperature response rates and parameters for individual species within each study. Temperature response rates and parameters included in this meta-analysis are: the optimum temperature of light saturated photosynthesis (ToptA), the optimum temperature of photosynthetic electron transport (ToptJ), the optimum temperature of maximum Rubisco carboxylation, the rate of light saturated photosynthesis at 25C (A25), the rate of photosynthetic electron transport at 25C (J25), the rate of maximum Rubisco carboxylation at 25C (V25), the ratio of J25 to V25 (JV), the width of the photosynthetic temperature response curve, the activation energy term for photosynthetic electron transport (EaJ), and the activation energy term for maximum Rubisco carboxylation (EaV).
Rcode used to extract these parameters is provided.

We used latitude and longitude data provided by data authors to merge our dataset with climate variables extracted from the WorldClim database (Fick and Hijmans, 2017). Rcode used to extract data and combine with our datasets are provided in: "WorldClim_TerraClim_Extraction_4.10.22.Rmd" and "MetaAnalysis_DataEdit_Climate_3.11.24.Rmd" R Markdown files.
Fick SE, Hijmans RJ. 2017. WorldClim 2: new 1-km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology 37: 4302–4312.
All statistical analyses are provided in R.
